messages:
alice: starting thread to capture the postmortem notes and action items from last night's hosted inference spike. we had a ~45m window where a subset of requests returned 5xx/gateway timeouts; customer impact was mostly timeouts on >2s tail which caused retries and some billing complaints. putting everything here so we can assign owners and track follow-ups.

ben: timeline summary from observability: around 2026-03-14T22:12:00Z we saw a sudden increase in queue depth for the hosted-gateway frontends serving inference-hosted-us-east-1. error rate (5xx) from 0.2% to 7.8% in ~3 minutes, CPU on the router pods spiked and we hit connection pool exhaustion to backend inference workers. autoscaler didn't trigger fast enough for the particular worker pool due to a mispredicted scale-down window. mitigation at 22:28 involved routing ~25% of requests to canary-region and applying temporary rate-limits for high-throughput customers.

carol: root cause hypothesis: a recent change in the request router (PR #4127) introduced a per-connection keepalive change that reduced the effective connection pool size when clients used http/1.1 with many short-lived connections. combined with a hot set of inference model requests (longer seq len), KV cache misses, and a burst from a marketing campaign, we overwhelmed the worker pool.

david: reproduction steps we used in staging: 1) spawn 2500 concurrent short-lived connections with sequence length distribution skewed to 512 tokens; 2) ensure KV cache disabled; 3) run against router image sha: `sha256:3af9b2c`; observed the same 502s on the router and `connection refused` errors in worker logs. snippet: ```bash
wrk -t100 -c2500 -d180s --latency http://router-us-east-1.internal/v1/generate -s scripts/long_seq.lua
```

maria: customer-facing impact: support received ~18 escalations, sample diffs show many reported timeouts and duplicate charges due to client-side retries. we've paused billing adjustments pending full postmortem. support-bot can dump ticket ids later. @support-bot can you attach top 5 affected org ids?

support-bot: attached org ids: org_88a, org_cf4, org_b3d, org_9ee, org_22f. flagged for CS outreach.

julian: quick mitigation notes: we reverted the router change at 22:35 (rolled back PR #4127), increased router pod replicas by 30% in us-east, temporarily lowered default per-org concurrency limit to 75% for the heavy-tenants, and enabled a secondary fallback path that sends low-priority traffic to quantized-model variants. latency normalized by ~22:46.

alice: good. now action items (concrete, owners, due dates):
- "router-keepalive-regression": revert PR stabilized but need permanent fix. owner: ben. due: 2026-03-21. description: add unit/integration tests that simulate many short-lived http/1.1 connections and validate effective pool size; run against router on canary.
- "autoscaler-tuning": owner: carol. due: 2026-03-18. description: adjust scale-up thresholds for inference worker pools, reduce cooldown on scale-up path, and add a fast-path when queue depth delta > 200/s. include load tests that mimic marketing-burst profile.
- "circuit-breaker-by-org": owner: julian. due: 2026-03-16. description: implement soft circuit-breaker that temporarily reduces routing weight for orgs that exceed sustained token-per-second thresholds. add dashboards for per-org backpressure.
- "billing-retry-protections": owner: maria. due: 2026-03-17. description: coordinate with billing to ensure retries within 60s are deduped; produce customer communication template for affected orgs.
- "end-to-end-regression-test": owner: david. due: 2026-03-22. description: new e2e test that includes KV cache cold-start + long sequences + HTTP/1.1 short connections, run in CI nightlies and before router changes land. include the exact `wrk` script and data seed.
- "obs-alerting-improvement": owner: alice. due: 2026-03-15. description: add a composite alert that triggers when router 5xx > 1% AND queue depth > 100 for > 2m, with automatic paging to oncall. include synthetic canary probes to detect connection pool degradation.

ben: technical notes for the fix: keepalive defaults need to be signal-safe across our threadpool. switching back to previous behavior was fine as an emergency but we need to model connection teardown rates. propose adding a metric `router.conn_pool.available` and surface it in the console. also patch PR #4127 with a feature-flag guarded change and a compatibility mode for http/1.1 clients.

carol: autoscaler details: current HPA uses cpu and custom queue_length metric with a 3m window. we should add a short-window emergency metric (30s) and a predictive smoothing to account for burstiness. I'll draft proposed config and run it in staging for 48h.

julian: on the fallback model routing: we need to be careful about quality regressions. added an opt-in flag for orgs so they can opt out of fallback quantized variants; default remains on for best-effort during incidents. ops-bot will record which orgs were routed to fallback.

maria: for customers and billing: recommend proactive refund offer for the top 5 orgs and a status post with timeline. drafting language now, will share with CS for approvals.

alice: follow-up meeting scheduled: 2026-03-16 16:00 UTC in #incidents-review. agenda: verify fixes, confirm test coverage, customer outreach plan, and retro. please add any other items.

david: logs to attach for the postmortem: router logs (22:05-22:55), worker pool logs, autoscaler metrics, and the `wrk` reproduction run outputs. I'll upload to the incident bucket and post link.

support-bot: incident bucket links: s3://redwood-incidents/1793507777/router-logs.tar.gz , s3://redwood-incidents/1793507777/worker-logs.tar.gz , s3://redwood-incidents/1793507777/autoscaler-metrics.csv

alice: outstanding questions: 1) do we want to change default per-org concurrency now or only during incidents? 2) are there any customers who must not be routed to quantized fallback? please call out in thread.

carol: opinion: prefer not to change default for everyone; implement per-org overrides and make default safer (slightly lower) in the short term.

maria: i'll collate the list of customers with strict SLAs and share by EOD.

ben: I'll open PRs for the router metric and the feature-flagged retry and link them here. PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/router/pull/4182 and https://github.com/redwood-inference/router/pull/4183

alice: thanks all. assigning owners in the ticket tracker now. please update the ticket with progress and mark items done before the follow-up meeting. :thumbsup:
